answer: Requiring agents to post a refundable stake before they can trade turns a Sybil flood into a costly canyon to cross: each fake identity must lock real funds, so a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. Honest agents earn their stake back plus fees, while detected fakes lose it. Reputation then becomes a bridge between stake and trust: past honest work raises an agent's standing at dawn of each new epoch, while fresh, unproven identities start throttled until they prove themselves.
